instruction: Change the system clock to use 12-hour AM/PM format.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened GNOME Settings, navigated to Date & Time, opened the timezone map picker, searched for 'London', and changed timezone from HKT (UTC+8) to GMT (UTC+0) in 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open GNOME Settings, navigate sidebar sections, interact with Date & Time settings, use timezone map search, select timezone from results, modify system settings
metadata.task_rationale: Agent demonstrated ability to navigate GNOME Date & Time settings. Changing clock format to 12-hour is a related setting on the same panel, testing the model's ability to find and toggle a different option.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing clock display format from 24-hour to 12-hour AM/PM. Evaluator checks gsettings clock-format value contains '12h'. The setting is on the same Date & Time panel the agent already navigated to successfully.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-format' to extract the GNOME clock format setting, which is the authoritative source for this configuration.
Metric check_include_exclude correctly checks that the output contains '12h', which is the expected gsettings value for 12-hour format.
Single-requirement instruction (change to 12-hour format) is fully covered by the single evaluator check.
No postconfig needed since gsettings is a command-line query that reads persistent dconf state, not UI-dependent.
